cases.query: after a larger KRN kernel migration slice should Codex ask Claude for second opinion or just close the work

priorSession.task: Refine the second-opinion-claude skill after a larger KRN kernel slice and record the governed review loop as learned operating evidence.

memoryCards.title: Second opinion after larger KRN slice
memoryCards.summary: After larger migrations or audit-hardening slices, Codex owns a governed second-opinion-Claude loop with acceptance criteria, verification evidence, diff freshness, and explicit triage before closing.
memoryCards.falsifier: A large KRN refactor closes from local tests only and never runs governed second-opinion review.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove Claude judgment is correct or that every tiny slice needs review.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN's operating loop requires governed Claude second opinion after larger migration or audit-hardening slices.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The second-opinion skill builds a compact context pack, requests read-only falsification, validates verdict JSON, and forces Codex-owned triage instead of operator coordination.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Large memory/kernel slices should not close until local evidence and governed second-opinion output have been reconciled.
sourceClaims.falsifier: The review output is prose-only, stale against the diff, or routed back to the operator as the default decision layer.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove second opinion is required for small deterministic eval fixture edits.

cases.query: when a slice changes KRN memory eval behavior what company review standard should Codex apply before closing

priorSession.task: A prior memory eval slice passed local tests but Claude found a proof overclaim, so Codex learned to reconcile reviewer evidence before closing.

memoryCards.title: Company review standard after memory eval change
memoryCards.summary: When a KRN memory eval slice changes behavior, Codex should verify focused tests, run the eval command, typecheck, diff-check, and reconcile Claude findings before closing.
memoryCards.falsifier: A memory eval behavior change closes with only a single unit test and no review evidence.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove the eval measures arbitrary agent quality.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN memory eval behavior changes require focused tests, eval command evidence, typecheck, diff-check, and reconciled second-opinion findings before closure.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The closure loop combines local deterministic checks with an independent falsification review and records proof/non-proof boundaries.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: A later slice that changes memory eval behavior should apply the learned closure standard rather than closing on one green assertion.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A later memory eval behavior change closes without focused eval evidence or reconciled review output.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove every documentation-only edit needs Claude review.

cases.query: months after the source authority fixes what rule should Codex remember about accepted SourceClaims in activation context

priorSession.task: Earlier source authority hardening taught that activation and source-search may treat only accepted SourceClaims as context authority.

memoryCards.title: Accepted SourceClaims only for authority
memoryCards.summary: KRN activation and source-search readbacks must exclude proposed, rejected, and deprecated SourceClaims before they can appear as authoritative context.
memoryCards.falsifier: A proposed or rejected SourceClaim appears as supporting context authority.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove accepted claims are true or decision-linked.

sourceClaims.claim: KRN activation and source-search authority is limited to accepted SourceClaims.
sourceClaims.mechanism: The authority filter excludes proposed, rejected, and deprecated claims before ContextROI or source-search support packaging.
sourceClaims.krnImplication: Long-range source authority recall should keep non-accepted claims out of implementation context.
sourceClaims.falsifier: A non-accepted claim survives as a source-search supporting claim or context inclusion.
sourceClaims.doesNotProve: This does not prove source truth or ranking quality.

cases.query: for a larger KRN migration should Codex follow the old no second opinion rule from before the governed reviewer existed

priorSession.task: An old workflow note said larger slices could close without second opinion, but later review reversed it.

memoryCards.title: Routine dependency pin cleanup
memoryCards.summary: For a small package metadata cleanup, local deterministic tests and typecheck are enough evidence when no kernel behavior changes.
memoryCards.falsifier: The slice changes memory, source, activation, or evaluation behavior.
memoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not apply to behavior-changing evaluation work.

excludedMemoryCards.title: Obsolete no second opinion rule
excludedMemoryCards.summary: Old guidance said Codex may close larger KRN migrations from local tests only without a governed second opinion loop.
excludedMemoryCards.falsifier: The governed second-opinion skill is available and required by the current operating loop.
excludedMemoryCards.doesNotProve: This does not prove every tiny deterministic edit needs review.
excludedMemoryCards.exclusionReason: stale memory contradicted by later governed second-opinion operating rule
